cohort: 500 consecutive new and follow-up secondary care IBS outpatients (399 female, 101 male, age range 15-87, mean age 46) fulfilling Rome III criteria without any significant concomitant disease
finding: The prevalence of fecal incontinence in this cohort of relatively young IBS patients was high (57%), approaching that observed in elderly care homes, and was present even in those with constipation-predominant IBS.
